analysis.investment_thesis: Datamatics fails both Magic Formula screens simultaneously: earnings yield of ~5.3% (EBIT 232 Cr / EV ~4,392 Cr) is below the 6% minimum threshold, and ROIC of ~17% falls short of the 20%+ required for a genuinely good business. At 20x earnings for a single-digit revenue grower with declining operating income, the market is not offering a bargain.
key_strengths: FCF conversion is strong — FCF 201 Cr nearly equals net profit 206 Cr (2025), confirming low capex intensity
Consistent profitability over 9 years with net profit CAGR of 18.4% driven by margin expansion
Low leverage (D/E 0.13 pre-2025) and 66% promoter holding provide stability
key_risks: Operating income actually DECLINED from 246 Cr (2024) to 232 Cr (2025) despite revenue growing — margin compression is real
Debt-funded acquisition in FY25 spiked borrowings from 17 Cr to 186 Cr and total assets +47%; goodwill dilutes true ROIC
Other income surged to 78 Cr (38% of operating profit) in FY25 — net profit quality is weak; strip it out and earnings look far lower
red_flags: Operating margin contracting: EBITDA peaked at 271 Cr (2023), fell to 264 Cr (2024), 256 Cr (2025) — wrong direction
Earnings yield ~5.3% is below Magic Formula's minimum 6% hurdle — stock is overvalued on this metric
FII ownership at 0.48% — sophisticated global capital is conspicuously absent
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula numbers: EBIT (operating income) = INR 232 Cr for FY25. EV = Market Cap 4,420 + Debt 190 − Cash 218 = ~4,392 Cr. Earnings yield = 232/4,392 = **5.3%** — below the 6% floor I require. For ROIC, using invested capital of ~1,400 Cr (equity + debt − cash, adjusted for the acquisition bump), ROIC ≈ **16–17%** — decent but below my 20% threshold for a "good" business. When BOTH metrics miss, the Magic Formula gives no reason to buy.

The business narrative is further complicated by deteriorating operating trends. Revenue grew 11% in FY25, yet operating income fell 5.7% — margins are compressing. The 78 Cr in other income is propping up the 206 Cr net profit; stripping it out yields an adjusted PAT closer to 150 Cr, implying a true P/E above 29x. The FY25 debt-funded acquisition (total assets up 700 Cr, borrowings up 169 Cr) introduces integration risk and makes future ROIC harder to gauge. Revenue CAGR of just 8.7% over 9 years does not justify the premium multiple. HOLD or revisit only if price drops to ~INR 450–500 (earnings yield >8%) and operating margins stabilise.
